paragraphs: Fostering for Sandwell's children is run by Sandwell Children's Trust, a not-for-profit company that took over the service from Sandwell Council and is registered as an independent fostering agency under the name Foster Sandwell. It recruits carers only for children known to the Trust and works only in Sandwell. The independent agencies listed below also cover the borough.

The Trust's statement of purpose lists short-term, long-term, emergency, respite, parent and child, fostering for adoption, family and friends care and staying put after 18, as well as specialist placements for children stepping down from residential care. In January 2026 it ran a Foster Sandwell recruitment campaign with posters across the borough and information events in Oldbury, Rowley Regis, Smethwick and West Bromwich. Sandwell Council reported that the fostering service is rated Good by Ofsted.

Carers receive a fortnightly allowance, and the Trust publishes its fees, allowances and discount schemes for carers on its website. Each household has a supervising social worker who visits at least every eight weeks, with monthly support groups, quarterly coffee mornings, FosterTalk membership and out-of-hours help from the emergency duty team. Skills to Foster training comes before approval, with core courses in the first year.

The process starts with an information pack and an enquiry form, then an information event and a home visit before you apply. The Trust aims to complete the assessment in about 16 weeks before your case goes to the fostering panel. Foster Sandwell's number is 0800 358 0899. It is worth speaking to two or three of the services on this page before choosing.
